name: 99 Minutos
description: 99minutos (99 Minutos) is a Latin American last-mile logistics and delivery platform serving ecommerce businesses across Mexico, Chile, Colombia and Peru. It offers express parcel delivery (envios99), full-truck-load and drayage freight (freight99), fulfillment and warehousing (fulfill99) and custom logistics operations (tailor99), backed by a network of pickup/delivery points (Punto99). Its public REST API v3 lets developers resolve addresses to reusable location ids, quote shipping rates and coverage, create/confirm orders (including multibox), print PDF and ZPL labels, track shipments and subscribe to real-time status webhooks. Authentication is OAuth2 client-credentials that returns a bearer JWT. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from the provider's own developer portal.

name: Aora
description: Aora (Aora Servicios) is a Mexico-based on-demand home and office services marketplace that connects households and businesses with vetted technicians and providers for repairs, installations, and maintenance. Its catalog spans home and office repairs, white-goods and appliance service, air conditioning and mini-split installation, water heaters, plumbing and drainage, waterproofing, and home-technology work. Consumers browse and book services through the Aora web app and the Aora mobile app, while a B2B program serves business customers. The company is backed by 500 Global. Aora publishes a consumer-facing website and blog but does not currently expose a public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs; this profile captures its public web surface and domain-security posture.

name: Aplazo
description: Aplazo is a Mexican buy now, pay later (BNPL) payment platform that lets shoppers split online and in-store purchases into installments without a credit card, paying over time directly from their bank account. For merchants, Aplazo exposes a REST payment API (api.aplazo.mx) and official e-commerce plugins (Magento 2, VTEX, Shopify, PrestaShop, Tiendanube) to originate loans at checkout, retrieve loan status, and process refunds and cancellations. Merchants authenticate with an apiToken and merchantId to obtain a short-lived JWT bearer token, then create loans that redirect the customer to Aplazo to complete financing. Aplazo is backed by QED Investors and operates in Mexico, settling in Mexican pesos (MXN).

name: Arq
description: Arq (formerly DolarApp) is a Latin American cross-border fintech app that gives travelers, investors, and professionals digital dollar and digital euro accounts at real market rates without hidden fees. Founded in 2021, the mobile-first platform offers currency conversion, a borderless payment card, global accounts to send and receive international payments, bill payment, PIX transfers, stock and ETF investing, and high-yield Trade and Save accounts, plus ARQ Premium and Prestige tiers. Arq raised $70M from Sequoia Capital and Founders Fund and serves over 2 million users across the Americas. Arq is a consumer mobile product and does not publish a public API or developer portal; this profile captures its verified public identity and web surface for the API Evangelist network.

name: AstroPay
description: AstroPay is a Uruguay-founded fintech and electronic money institution offering a multicurrency wallet, virtual and physical AstroCards, FX, and cross-border money transfers for consumers across Latin America, plus a business platform that lets merchants accept payments, issue cards, manage payroll, and pay out to wallets and bank accounts. AstroPay is regulated as an EMI in the UK, Denmark, Isle of Man, and Brazil, and operates the AstroPay wallet across Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Mexico, Peru, Colombia, Uruguay, and additional global corridors with support for ARS, BRL, CLP, COP, EUR, GBP, MXN, PEN, USD, USDT, and UYU. For developers, AstroPay exposes a comprehensive REST platform spanning payments, payouts, PIX instant payments in Brazil, issued cards, savings accounts, scheme transfers, user account management, tokenization (PCI-compliant card collection), settlements, transaction reporting, hosted and embedded Checkout, QR-code POS, Wallet-on-File account linking, Cashouts, and Webhooks — accessed through `developers.astropay.com` with HMAC-signed callbacks and an OAuth/API-key authentication model.

name: Atrato
description: Atrato (Atrato Technologies S.A.P.I. de C.V., atratopago.com) is a Mexican fintech offering buy-now-pay-later (BNPL) point-of-sale financing. Affiliated merchants let shoppers split purchases of up to $200,000 MXN into installments of up to 24 months, without a credit or debit card, with approval in minutes. Atrato serves furniture, healthcare, mobility, construction, motorcycle, appliance and other verticals, and is regulated by PROFECO. Its Atrato Partners platform exposes a REST integration API (api-partners) covering in-store cash-in payment collection and ecommerce checkout order generation, plus status/disbursement webhooks and WooCommerce, Shopify and Magento plugins. This profile was enriched from Atrato's public developer documentation at docs.atratopago.com.

name: AutoChilango
description: AutoChilango (Auto Chilango) is a Mexico City-based mobile application that consolidates the everyday services drivers in CDMX and the State of Mexico need into a single app. It covers the "Hoy No Circula" driving-restriction calendar, vehicular verification schedules, traffic fines (multas) lookup and payment, annual registration (tenencia), insurance, parking, gas stations, and mechanical services for private cars, motorcycles, taxis, and special plates. Backed by 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer/API surface has been found, so this profile captures the provider's identity, information surface (blog, FAQs, privacy), and probed domain security.

name: Aviva
description: Aviva (Aviva Financial, S.A. de C.V., SOFOM E.N.R.) is a Mexican fintech lender operating under the tagline "Tu historia importa." It offers quick, secured personal and business loans originated in person through a network of 100+ physical kiosks across central Mexico (Puebla, Hidalgo, Estado de Mexico, Morelos, Queretaro, Tlaxcala and Veracruz), using a video-call onboarding flow (the Aviva Onboarding System, AOS) with same-day or 24-hour direct-deposit disbursement. Products include Aviva Contigo (everyday expenses, up to $15,000), Aviva tu Negocio (business owners, up to $20,000), Aviva tu Compra (appliances at Bodega Aurrera), and Aviva tu Casa (construction materials via Construrama). Borrowers manage payments through the Aviva mobile app. Aviva was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Aviva publishes no public developer portal, API, SDKs, or OpenAPI - it exposes a consumer web/app and kiosk surface only.

name: Baubap
description: Baubap is a Mexican fintech offering instant personal microloans through an Android mobile app. Founded in 2018 in Mexico City by Roberto Salcedo and Luis Villarreal, it grants loans from $500 to roughly $9,000 MXN in minutes with no credit-bureau check and no income verification, using its own AI/ML-based alternative-scoring model to serve underbanked and no-credit-history borrowers. On-time repayment unlocks progressively larger amounts and helps users build a positive credit history. Baubap operates as a regulated SOFOM registered with CONDUSEF and supervised by CNBV, complying with Mexican data-protection and financial-security regulations. It has no public developer API; this profile captures the company's identity, its published /llms.txt, and its domain-security posture.

name: BBVA
description: BBVA is a multinational Spanish financial services group operating in over 30 countries. The BBVA API Market provides a comprehensive catalog of banking APIs covering accounts, payments, collections, financing, identity, and open data across Spain, Mexico, Latin America, and other global markets. BBVA is a recognized open banking leader offering PSD2-compliant APIs, treasury management solutions, and digital ecosystem integrations.

name: Bitso
description: Bitso is one of Latin America's largest cryptocurrency exchanges and stablecoin-rail providers, serving Mexico, Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, and other LATAM markets. Bitso exposes a public REST trading API and a WebSocket feed at bitso.com/api/v3 for market data, order management, conversions, OTC / RFQ, and account operations; a Payouts & Pay-Ins API for cross-border crypto and fiat disbursements; and the Juno API for Mexican peso (MXN) rails and stablecoin programmable money. API and OpenAPI references are catalogued at docs.bitso.com.

name: Bright
description: Bright is Mexico's leading residential and commercial solar energy provider, founded in 2014 (Y Combinator W15) by Jonah Greenberger. Often described as "Sunrun for the developing world," Bright combines financing and software to let homeowners and businesses adopt rooftop solar and battery energy storage (BESS) at no upfront cost. The company operates a marketplace connecting a network of local installers, distributors, and retail promoters with customers, and offers financing models such as solar PPAs and leasing schemes. Bright's public web presence is a Wix-hosted marketing site (thinkbright.mx) covering its industrial, commercial, and home solutions, success cases, and 24/7 energy monitoring technology. It exposes an agent-facing surface via an llms.txt and a hosted Wix Site MCP endpoint, but publishes no first-party developer/REST API.

name: Calificadas
description: Calificadas is a Mexico-based, AI-powered human development company that combines artificial intelligence, strategic consulting, and training to help organizations and teams adapt to rapid change. Its tagline is "human infrastructure for the era of artificial intelligence." Its flagship product, CUALY (cualy.tech), is an AI-native platform for developing human capabilities through diagnosis, personalization, and continuous AI-driven feedback across communication, leadership, and collaboration, using voice and video analysis and AI coaches, plus organizational dashboards and iOS/Android apps. The company also delivers organizational consulting, leadership training, and adaptive training programs, and counts Coca-Cola FEMSA, ManpowerGroup, and Alsea among its clients. Backed by 500 Global, Calificadas was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, or API documentation; artifacts below reflect its public web and domain-security surface only.

name: Circulo de Belleza
description: Círculo de Belleza is an authorized distributor of professional beauty products in Mexico, operating an e-commerce storefront at circulodebelleza.com. It sells salon-quality hair care, hair color, nail, barbershop, and facial/spa supplies from 40+ professional brands (L'Oréal Professionnel, Olaplex, Wella, Schwarzkopf, Matrix, Alfaparf Milano) at professional pricing with no minimum purchase, same-day fulfillment, and nationwide Mexico delivery. The store is built on Shopify and exposes a native agent-commerce surface: a published llms.txt/agents.md, OpenID Connect and OAuth authorization-server discovery documents, and a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) MCP endpoint for agent-driven catalog search, cart, and buyer-approved checkout.

name: Civica Digital
description: Cívica Digital is a Mexican civic-technology company, founded in 2015 and backed by 500 Global, that helps governments, public institutions, and organizations design, build, and launch digital services for citizens. Its product portfolio includes Urbem, a platform for digitizing government procedures and citizen-facing services; Signum, a digital document and official-records management system with electronic signatures; and a suite of conversational AI agents that support citizens over WhatsApp, phone, and web. The company focuses on digital government transformation across Latin America. No public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface has been located; this profile captures the company's public web presence, legal pages, and domain-security posture.

name: Clip
description: Clip (legal name Payclip) is a Mexico City-based fintech and SMB acquirer often described as the Square equivalent in Mexico. Founded in 2012, Clip enables merchants of all sizes to accept card, contactless, and QR payments through a family of mobile point-of-sale (mPOS) terminals — Clip Plus 2, Clip Pro 2, Clip Ultra, Clip Total 3, and the high-volume Clip PinPad — as well as Tap to Pay on iOS/Android smartphones, an online Checkout payment gateway, payment links, and the Clip Cuenta digital business account with same-day settlement and SMB loans. Clip operates the developer portal developer.clip.mx, which publishes the Checkout Redirect, Checkout Transparente, Transactions, Deposits, Refunds, and PinPad APIs along with the Checkout Transparente SDK and a Terminal SDK for embedding card acceptance into third-party POS apps. The company is backed by strategic investors including American Express Ventures, Banorte, Capital Group, and Morgan Stanley, and is consistently ranked among Mexico's top private fintech employers.

name: Cobre
description: Cobre is a Latin American B2B payments and treasury platform that gives finance teams, fintechs, PSPs and banks a single API and portal to move money in and out of Colombia and Mexico (and via Fedwire in the United States) and across borders. Its modular products cover Local Payments (Bre-B, Fast Pay, ACH and PSE in Colombia; SPEI and CLABEs in Mexico), Cross Border Payments with FX quotes, Global Payouts in stablecoins, and Connect for centralizing and reconciling bank accounts. The developer API is a REST platform (v1) with bearer-JWT auth via a credential exchange, required idempotency on money movements, page-based pagination, a 30 TPS rate limit, HMAC-signed webhook notifications, and a full portal for maker-checker approvals, reconciliation and reporting. Cobre is a QED Investors portfolio company.

name: Come Bien
description: Come Bien is a Mexican foodtech company operating a digital corporate cafeteria (comedor digital) that delivers fresh, home-style, nutritionally balanced meals to offices without requiring any on-site kitchen installation. Employees choose from a rotating seven-week cyclical menu each day, place their order through the Come Bien app, and receive individually bagged, ready-to-eat meals delivered to the workplace in 100% biodegradable packaging. A dedicated backoffice platform lets employers subsidize, administer, and gain full visibility into their team's food benefit. Backed by 500 Global, the company reports serving 100+ companies, 10,000+ employees, and more than 1.5M orders delivered.

name: Cometa
description: Cometa (getcometa.com / cometaedu.com) is a Mexican education technology company that provides an operating system for private schools. More than 500 private schools in Mexico use Cometa to run and automate their operations across a set of integrated modules: Cobranzas (tuition collections with WhatsApp and email payment reminders and dashboards), Tienda en linea (an online store for uniforms, materials and services with vendor management), Admisiones y Reinscripciones (admissions and re-enrollment workflows), Comunicaciones (AI-assisted, multi-channel family communications with engagement analytics), Calificaciones (grade entry and SEP-compliant report cards and digital credentials), and Gestion Escolar (attendance, incident logging and administrative workflows). Cometa is a 500 Global portfolio company. It was surfaced as a stub in the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this pass Cometa publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API documentation surface.

name: Conekta
description: Conekta is a Mexico-based payment processor that lets businesses accept credit and debit cards, OXXO cash vouchers, SPEI bank transfers, Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Buy Now Pay Later through a single PCI-DSS Level 1 certified API. The platform serves the Mexican market with Spanish-language documentation, CNBV-aligned compliance, and full Orders, Charges, Customers, Subscriptions, Payment Links, Antifraud, Webhooks, Payouts, and Balances resources. Conekta publishes its OpenAPI 3.1 specification publicly under MIT license, ships official SDKs for PHP, Node.js, Python, Ruby, .NET, and Java, and offers mobile components for Android, iOS, Flutter, and React Native plus plugins for major e-commerce platforms.

name: Contalink
description: Contalink is a Mexican cloud accounting and payroll platform ("contabilidad en la nube") built for independent accountants, accounting firms (despachos) and SMEs. It automates repetitive Mexican fiscal work — bulk CFDI download and classification, electronic accounting, DIOT preparation, treasury and bank reconciliation, invoicing (facturación) and payroll (nómina) with digital stamping — across multiple companies and users. Contalink also exposes a REST API that lets external systems read and post accounting data: trial balance (balanza de comprobación), account balances, manual accounting policies (pólizas manuales), invoice reconciliation (conciliación), bank transactions (movimientos bancarios) and CFDI fiscal-document listing, upload and status checks. The API authenticates with a per-company API key sent in the Authorization header. Backed by 500 Global.

name: Cornershop by Uber
description: Cornershop is an on-demand grocery and essentials delivery service founded in 2015 in Chile by Oskar Hjertonsson, Daniel Undurraga, and Juan Pablo Cuevas, simultaneously launching in Santiago, Chile and Mexico City, Mexico. The platform connects consumers with personal shoppers who pick and deliver groceries, pharmacy items, and other goods from local supermarkets, specialty stores, and big-box retailers. After a 2018 acquisition attempt by Walmart was blocked by Mexican regulators, Uber agreed in October 2019 to acquire majority ownership, completing full acquisition in July 2021 at a reported valuation north of US$3 billion — Chile's first unicorn exit. At its peak Cornershop operated in eight countries across the Americas: Chile, Mexico, Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Peru, Canada, and the United States. Beginning in 2021 Uber merged the Cornershop brand into Uber Eats, migrating the grocery vertical ("Uber Eats Grocery") into its main consumer app and progressively shutting down the standalone Cornershop apps and websites. As of 2026 cornershopapp.com and cornershop.io redirect to ubereats.com, the Cornershop LLC GitHub organization (archived October 2024) has zero public repositories, and there is no public developer API, SDK, partner program, or technical documentation under the Cornershop brand — Cornershop survives only as engineering history and as the LatAm backbone of Uber Eats Grocery. Community-built unofficial Python wrappers exist on GitHub but reverse-engineer the consumer mobile app and are not sanctioned by Uber.

name: Covalto
description: Covalto (formerly Credijusto) is a Mexican digital bank for small and medium-sized businesses, headquartered in Mexico City. It offers business and personal checking accounts, fixed-rate investment products, quick working-capital credit (Agil Covalto), factoring, leasing (arrendamiento), and fiduciary trust services (fideicomisos). Covalto acquired a regulated Mexican banking license, making it one of the first fintechs in Mexico to become a fully licensed bank. Its digital surface spans online banking, digital account opening, and a credit application flow. Covalto is backed by QED Investors. As of the latest review it publishes no public API developer portal; its developer documentation at docs.covalto.com is gated behind Google Identity-Aware Proxy for internal use.

name: Cuenca
description: Cuenca is a Mexican fintech (challenger bank / neobank) founded in 2018 that offers a banking-as-a-service REST API for moving money in Mexico. The API at api.cuenca.com covers SPEI and internal transfers, deposits, CLABE account provisioning, debit card issuing (physical and virtual), card transactions, bill payments to service providers, balances, statements, commissions, and KYC / identity validation (CURP validation, identity verification, KYC checks). It authenticates with an API key plus secret (HTTP basic), optional short-lived JWTs, and login / session tokens, exposes a sandbox at sandbox.cuenca.com, signs transfers with an idempotency key, paginates with a cursor (next_page_uri), and pushes webhooks for transaction, card, deposit and user events. Official client libraries ship for Python (cuenca) and Java (CuencaJava), with open-source tooling for CLABE validation and CEP receipts under the cuenca-mx GitHub organization.

name: Cuida Mi Mascota
description: Cuida Mi Mascota (CuidaMiMascota SAPI de CV) is a Mexican pet-care marketplace that connects pet owners with vetted, trusted caregivers for boarding (hospedaje), daycare, in-home visits, and dog walking across cities in Mexico. Delivered primarily as consumer iOS and Android mobile apps, the platform has served more than 250,000 pet owners and lets caregivers register to offer services. It is a 500 Global portfolio company. The company exposes no public API, developer portal, or SDK today; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company lead with identity and domain-security signals captured for discovery.

name: Custodian
description: Custodian (getcustodian.com) is a Mexico City-based consumer mobile application and insurtech service that centralizes vehicle documentation and automotive administrative tasks. The app helps drivers organize and store important paperwork, track expiration dates for registration, insurance policies, and health certificates, receive renewal notifications, and get assistance with auto-insurance renewals and claims management. A premium annual subscription (450 MXN) adds full document-handling and verification services (including Mexico City vehicle verification). Custodian is a consumer app distributed via the Apple App Store and Google Play; it does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI at this time. Backed by 500 Global.

name: datos.gob.mx - Sitio oficial de datos abiertos del Gobierno de la República
description: datos.gob.mx - Sitio oficial de datos abiertos del Gobierno de la República is a open data portal open-data portal for Mexico running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 1,652 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

name: DeporPrivé
description: DeporPrivé is a Mexico-based sports e-commerce platform operating as a members-oriented "Sport Experience & Outlet" that runs flash sales and private, time-limited shopping events across more than 300 athletic brands including Adidas, Nike, and Salomon, with discounts reaching up to 70%. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in Mexico, the company curates footwear, apparel, and accessories for running, cycling, swimming, football, and general fitness, and has grown into one of the largest sport-specific online retailers in the country, fulfilling around 1,000 packages per day across multiple sales channels. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global. No public developer program, API, or documentation surface has been identified for this consumer retail brand.

name: Draftea
description: Draftea is a Mexico-based daily fantasy sports and real-money sports gaming platform, billed as the first daily fantasy sports (DFS) product for the Spanish-speaking world. Fans draft lineups of real athletes across soccer, American football (via an NFL partnership), basketball, baseball, and Formula 1, enter paid contests, and compete against other users for cash prizes rather than against a bookmaker. The company operates in Mexico under regulatory approval (DGAJS/SCEVF/P-06/2005-TER), distributes through native iOS and Android apps, and is backed by Sequoia, Kaszek, Bullpen Capital, Stepstone Group, and Courtside Ventures, along with athlete investors. Draftea is a consumer product company and does not currently publish a public developer API program; this profile captures its public web, support, legal, and open-source engineering surface.

name: EFEX (Ventu)
description: EFEX (efex.com, formerly efexpay.com) is a cross-border payments and treasury fintech serving businesses across the Americas. It enables international transfers to 140+ countries, bulk and mass payouts for payroll and multi-beneficiary disbursement, multi-currency business accounts (USD, MXN, EUR, GBP, CAD, JPY), international collections in local currency across 24+ countries, and FX and currency management for treasury optimization. Headquartered in Palo Alto, California with operations across Mexico (Mexico City, Monterrey, Tijuana, Queretaro, Guadalajara) and Colombia, EFEX is authorized by Mexico's CNBV as a money transmitter (registration 22469) and regulated by FinCEN in the United States. Backed by 500 Global. As of this profile the company exposes a business web/app product but no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

name: Expansive
description: Expansive is a Mexican real estate crowdfunding platform (crowdfunding inmobiliario) that lets individuals invest collectively in vetted real estate projects from as little as 1,000 MXN, earning returns backed by real guarantees. It operates as a regulated collective financing institution (IFC) under Mexico's Fintech Law and is supervised by the CNBV (Comisión Nacional Bancaria y de Valores). Expansive handles project vetting, funding, quarterly investor reporting, and payouts through its web platform and investor app (app.expansive.mx). The company is a portfolio company of 500 Global. It is a consumer-facing fintech investing product; it does not publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface.

name: Facturama
description: Facturama is a cloud-based Mexican electronic invoicing (CFDI) platform that lets businesses generate, stamp, download, and cancel digital tax receipts (Comprobante Fiscal Digital por Internet) through a REST API. It serves 55,000+ clients — mostly SMEs and startups — and exposes two API products: API Web (single issuer, tied to a Facturama account) and API Multiemisor (multi-issuer, for platforms that invoice on behalf of many taxpayers). The API supports CFDI 4.0 invoices, payroll receipts (nómina), payment complements (complemento de pago), credit notes, Carta Porte (cargo/transport), foreign trade (comercio exterior), and donation receipts, plus management of clients, products/services, branch offices, series, and SAT catalogs (postal codes, currencies, payment methods, tax regimes). Authentication is HTTP Basic. A sandbox environment and 15 free test invoices during a 30-day trial are available, along with first-party SDKs for PHP, Java, .NET, Node.js, JavaScript, Python, and Ruby and a public Postman collection.

name: Fairplay
description: Fairplay is a Mexican fintech offering flexible, collateral-free business financing for e-commerce sellers, marketplaces, retailers, and wholesalers. Its products include revolving credit lines (MXN 2-30 million), invoice advances/factoring, and working-capital financing, underwritten from a company's sales and analytics data with offers issued in as little as 48 hours through a 100% digital process. Fairplay operates as a Sociedad Financiera de Objeto Multiple, Entidad No Regulada (SOFOM E.N.R.) under Mexican CNBV and CONDUSEF supervision and is ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified for information security. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of QED Investors and Speedinvest. Fairplay serves financing and account data to customers through a private insights dashboard; no public developer API is currently published.

name: Gigstack
description: Gigstack (gigstack.pro) is a Mexican fintech and revenue-automation platform that automates electronic invoicing and tax compliance for businesses operating in Mexico. It generates CFDI 4.0 fiscal invoices through the SAT/PAC stamping pipeline, runs collections (cobranza) and accounts-receivable workflows, offers self-invoicing (autofactura) and customer portals, and performs automated SAT reconciliation and bulk SAT downloads (descarga masiva). Its REST API (v2, https://api.gigstack.io/v2) exposes clients, services, invoices (income/egress/draft/payment-complement), payments, receipts, retentions, teams, users, webhooks and SAT catalogs, with an official CLI and MCP server for terminal and agent workflows. Backed by 500 Global.

name: Gloset

name: Graviti
description: Graviti is a Mexico City-based consumer fintech founded in 2020 that unlocks affordable access to essential home utilities for unbanked and underserved Mexican families, starting with solar water heaters financed through a pay-as-you-go (PayGo / BNPL) model of small recurring payments. Backed by 500 Global, Clocktower Technology Ventures, Mucker Capital, Active Capital, and BFA Global's Catalyst Fund, the company combines hardware installation with embedded consumer lending. Graviti is a consumer-facing product company and does not publish a public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead and enriched with an honest no-API-surface result.

name: Healf
description: Healf (healf.mx) is a Mexico City-based InsurTech startup founded in 2022 that offers an AI-based SaaS platform to simplify, explain, and manage medical / health insurance policies. Using generative AI, natural language processing, and information-retrieval models, the platform automates repetitive inquiries, provides 24/7 conversational support to insurance brokers, and gives the insured comprehensive insight into their policy details for better-informed decisions. For brokers and doctors it streamlines communication and automates processes, improving transparency and traceability for insurers. Healf is a 500 Global portfolio company (Somos Lucha Batch 19), also backed by Blue Zone Ventures. This profile currently has no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification surface.

name: Kavak
description: Kavak is a Mexico-founded digital marketplace for buying, selling, and financing pre-owned cars across Latin America, the Middle East, and Turkey. Founded in 2016 in Mexico City by Carlos Garcia Ottati, Loreanne Garcia Ottati, and Roger Laughlin, Kavak became Mexico's first unicorn in 2020 and reached an $8.7B valuation in 2021 with backing from SoftBank, Sea Ltd, and Founders Fund. The company operates an end-to-end consumer platform that combines an e-commerce site and mobile app, physical hubs, in-house vehicle reconditioning, and a financial-services arm (Kavak Capital, Kuna, and Kavak Credito). Internally, Kavak uses machine learning and proprietary pricing models to value, inspect, and route inventory across markets including Mexico, Argentina, Brazil, Chile, the United Arab Emirates, and Turkey, while sponsoring high-profile partners such as the NFL. Kavak's revenue comes from vehicle sales, financing margins, and after-sales services, and the company does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or open-source GitHub organization. Customer-facing integrations are limited to the consumer web and mobile apps and partner financing channels.

name: Kayum
description: Kayum (KAYUM, S.A.P.I. de C.V.) is a Mexico City-based insurance data-analytics and software company serving the Mexican insurance market. It gives insurers exclusive, continuously updated market intelligence and actionable analysis: monthly price panels for GMM (major-medical), Life, and Auto lines backed by data from more than ten leading insurers, competitive pricing models, a quotation-processing tool (Claveteador) that compresses quote data preparation from days to minutes, customer-facing quoting platforms (Cotizadores) processing over 100,000 auto quotes a month, and compliance/document verification tooling (Suite 492 / ID Documental). Backed by 500 Global. The company publishes a marketing website but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

name: Klar
description: Klar is a Mexican digital financial services platform (neobank) headquartered in Mexico City with engineering in Berlin, serving roughly 7 million customers. Regulated by Mexico's CNBV, Klar offers a deposit account with yield, a no-annual-fee credit card, a secured (garantizada) credit card, the metal Platino card, personal loans, investment products, and Chubb-underwritten life and fraud insurance, plus cashback and interest-free-months (MSI) benefits. It also runs Klar Empresarial for business customers, partnered with Uber to launch the Uber Card in Mexico, and announced the acquisition of mortgage fintech Yave. Klar's product surface is delivered entirely through its consumer mobile app and website; as of this profile Klar publishes NO public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or sandbox, and no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, or webhook surface could be found. Third-party access to Klar accounts is generally brokered through Latin American open-finance aggregators (Belvo, Pluggy, Plaid) rather than a first-party Klar API. Klar does operate a public GitHub organization (klar-mx), but its repositories are internal infrastructure and DevOps tooling and forks, not client libraries for a Klar API.

name: Koltin
description: Koltin is a Mexican health membership company serving older adults, aimed at people aged roughly 50 to 84 and at the adult children who want to protect their parents and grandparents. Koltin is explicit that it is not an insurer and does not sell traditional policies: it packages access to private medical care, preventive follow-up, and financial protection against costly illness or accident into a membership. The membership pairs a major-medical expense insurance product operated and issued by BBVA Seguros Salud with preventive medicine — longevity assessments, an integrated medical check-up, video consultations, and continuous follow-up — plus a social community program (painting, tai chi, film discussion, dance). It operates across CDMX, Estado de Mexico, Guadalajara, Monterrey, Queretaro, Puebla, Guanajuato, Cuernavaca, Merida, and Veracruz, and publishes a member portal, a hospital network directory, and an extensive Spanish-language blog on aging and preventive health. Koltin is a 500 Global portfolio company. It publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification; it does publish a first-party llms.txt describing the site for language models.

name: Konfio
description: Konfio is a leading Mexican fintech serving small and medium businesses (SMBs) with an all-in-one platform: working-capital and term loans (Konfio Creditos), a business credit card (Konfio Tarjeta), payment terminals and acceptance (Konfio Pagos / Sirvis), and SMB management tools. Underwriting is powered by a proprietary algorithm that combines alternative data and ML to score creditworthiness in minutes. Konfio's product surface is overwhelmingly direct-to-SMB and the company does not publish a self-service public developer portal. Partner integrations (e.g. PayPal Working Capital, Goldman Sachs / Gramercy capital facilities, marketplace lending) are negotiated bilaterally.

name: Kushki
description: Kushki is an Ecuador-headquartered LatAm fintech operating as a regional non-banking acquirer for the Andean and Pacific Alliance markets — Ecuador, Colombia, Peru, Chile, Mexico, and Brazil. The Kushki API unifies card payments, scheduled and one-click subscriptions, bank transfers (PSE, Webpay Transferencia, SPEI, PIX), cash vouchers (OXXO, PagoEfectivo, Boleto), payouts/dispersions, and card-present (Kushki One POS) behind a single REST surface. Authentication is split across a Public-Merchant-Id (used in the browser to tokenize cards) and a Private-Merchant-Id (used server-side to charge). PCI DSS Level 1, 3DS 2.0, multi-layer anti-fraud, hosted fields, Kajita payment forms, Smartlinks, and e-commerce plugins (Shopify, VTEX, WooCommerce, Magento, PrestaShop) round out the platform.

name: Laureate Education
description: Laureate Education, Inc. is a for-profit higher-education network founded in 1989 as Sylvan Learning Systems and renamed Laureate Education in May 2004. At its 2017 IPO peak the company operated more than 200 campuses across 28 countries serving over one million students; it became only the third B Corporation to go public when it listed on NASDAQ (ticker: LAUR) on 1 February 2017. Between 2018 and 2021 Laureate executed one of the largest sector-wide divestiture programs in the history of higher education, exiting Brazil (sold to Ânima Holding for ~$765M), the United States (Walden University sold to Adtalem for $1.48B), Australia / New Zealand (sold to Strategic Education), Chile (Universidad Andrés Bello transferred to Fundación Educación y Cultura in September 2020), Spain, Portugal, Morocco, Turkey, Malaysia, China, Italy, Cyprus and the United Kingdom — returning $1.29B to shareholders in October 2021. After the divestiture cycle Laureate continued as a pure-play Mexico / Peru operator with five remaining institutions and approximately 460,000 students. In May 2024 the company was acquired by an investor group led by the International Finance Corporation (IFC, a member of the World Bank Group) and Sterling Capital, taking Laureate Education private and delisting it from NASDAQ. The company is headquartered at 1000 Brickell Avenue, Suite 715, Miami, FL.

name: Mattilda
description: Mattilda is a financial management platform for private educational institutions across Latin America, operating in Mexico, Colombia, and Ecuador. It automates tuition collection and payment processing, offers tuition advances that guarantee schools receive full monthly tuition on the first day regardless of family payment rates, and provides academic operations and admissions tools under its Algebraix product line. Families can pay through multiple channels, including WhatsApp. Mattilda operates under the oversight of Mexico's financial authorities CNBV and CONDUSEF and is backed by QED Investors. Mattilda does not currently expose a public developer API, SDKs, or documentation portal; this profile captures the company's public identity, status page, and Vanta-hosted trust center.

name: Mercado Pago
description: Mercado Pago is the payments and financial-services arm of Mercado Libre, Latin America's largest e-commerce and fintech platform. Founded in 2003, it processes a substantial share of LatAm digital payments across Brazil (PIX, Boleto, cards), Argentina, Mexico (SPEI, OXXO), Chile, Colombia, Peru, and Uruguay, with consumer wallet, merchant acquiring, card issuing, lending, and crypto products layered on top. The developer portal at developers.mercadopago.com exposes a deep payments stack — Checkout Pro (hosted), Checkout Bricks (composable web components), Checkout API (full server-side control), Orders API (next-gen checkout), Subscriptions, Payment Links, Point (in-person card readers), and QR payments — backed by REST APIs and official SDKs in Node.js / TypeScript, Python, PHP, Ruby, Java, .NET, Go, iOS, and Android, plus a CLI, an MCP server for AI agents, e-commerce plugins (WooCommerce, VTEX, Tiendanube, Shopify), and an n8n integration. Regional developer portals (.com.ar, .com.br, .com.mx, .com.cl, .com.co, .com.pe, .com.uy) localise docs and pricing per LATAM market.

Regional portals (.com.ar, .com.br, .com.mx, etc.) localise the docs and pricing per LATAM market.

name: Mienvío
description: Mienvío is a Mexican logistics control-tower platform that unifies multiple parcel carriers behind a single multi-carrier shipping API and dashboard for e-commerce, retail, marketplace, and fintech shippers across Latin America. It compares carrier rates, automates routing by cost, SLA, and coverage zone, generates shipping labels, and provides real-time tracking, delivery-incident management, and post-purchase customer notifications. Merchants integrate through the REST API (api.mienvio.mx/v2) or prebuilt Shopify and WooCommerce connectors, shipping nationally, internationally, and locally across Mexico, Colombia, Chile, Costa Rica, Peru, Guatemala, and El Salvador.

name: Minu Holdings Limited
description: Minu Holdings Limited operates minu.mx, Mexico's leading employee benefits and financial wellness platform. Minu provides employers with more than fifty benefits designed to attract, retain, and engage talent, including on-demand salary access (earned wage access), savings accounts, food and gas vouchers, payroll-linked loans, telemedicine, insurance, discounts, and financial education programs. Backed by 500 Global, Minu delivers these services to employees through its mobile app and integrates with employer payroll and HR systems. No public developer portal, API documentation, or OpenAPI specification was found during enrichment; the company operates a private/internal API surface (api.minu.mx responds but is not publicly documented).

name: Mision Admision
description: Misión Admisión is a Mexican education-technology company based in Mérida that prepares high school and university applicants for standardized admission exams such as EXANI I, EXANI II, PAA, and the UNAM, IPN, and UAM entrance tests. Its consumer web platform (misionadmision.com) delivers self-paced online courses, video lessons, interactive study capsules, thousands of practice questions, full-length exam simulators, live virtual and in-person classes, and the physical Sputnik smartbook guides. Founded in 2001 and online since 2015, the company is a seed-stage portfolio company of 500 Global. It is a consumer-facing EdTech platform and publishes no public developer API surface at this time; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for tracking and enrichment.

name: Mubit
description: Mubit is a temporary storage and logistics service based in Guadalajara, Mexico, offering on-demand collection, climate-controlled warehousing, digital photo inventory, and delivery for both individuals and businesses. Customers pay only for the space they use, with free pickup and drop-off, optional professional packing, and 24/7 CCTV-monitored facilities across three warehouses (Colli, Tijera, and Casuarina). Backed by 500 Global and Techstars, the company reports 4,000+ customers and a 4.9-star Google rating, and operates a mobile/web customer portal at clientes.mubit.co for scheduling pickups and deliveries and viewing stored items. Mubit publishes no public developer API.

name: Net Worth
description: netWorth (networth.mx) is a Mexico City fintech founded in 2016 and a 500 Startups (500 Global) Batch 10 company that helps individuals plan and manage retirement in Mexico. It specializes in Planes Personales de Retiro (PPR) and long-term savings and investment plans, combining human financial advisors (asesores) with digital tools such as retirement calculators and simulators, and commercializes plans backed by insurers and financial institutions such as Allianz and Skandia (Optimaxx Plus). The consumer product surfaces are a Webflow marketing site plus a client app at retiro.networth.mx and an authenticated portal at api.networth.mx; there is no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK program at this time.

name: Nu (Nubank)
description: Nu Holdings (Nubank) is Latin America's largest digital bank, with tens of millions of customers across Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia. Its core product surface - credit card, account, lending, investments, and insurance - is consumer-facing through the Nu mobile app, and Nubank does not publish a general-purpose public developer portal. Nubank participates in Brazil's Open Finance (Open Banking Brasil) regime, which standardises consent-driven access to account, transaction, and payment-initiation APIs for authorised third parties; Nubank's Open Finance endpoints are registered with the Brazilian Central Bank's directory. For merchant acceptance, Nubank operates NuPay for Business, a REST API for checkout payments, refunds, OAuth2/CIBA-based authorization, beneficiary management, and webhook event notifications, hosted at api.spinpay.com.br.

name: Pacto
description: Pacto is a Mexican fintech company modernizing payment acquisition for banks and hospitality businesses, moving them "de lo legacy a lo digital" (from legacy to digital). Pacto builds point-of-sale (POS) software and payment terminals: a miniPOS terminal and "Ordena y Paga" (order-and-pay) terminals plus value-added modules for banks, and a full restaurant POS suite (Pacto POS, Pacto GetNet, Order & Pay QR ordering, bill splitting, inventory, and reporting) for restaurants, cafes, bars, and fast-food counters. Backed by 500 Global and Banco Santander's GetNet, Pacto helps traditional financial institutions and merchants accept digital card payments and manage operations. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company; Pacto publishes a marketing site, blog, and pricing but no public developer API or documentation at this time.

name: Plenna
description: Plenna is a women's healthcare provider operating a network of integrated medical clinics across Mexico City, redefining health for women across every life stage. Its services span gynecology, maternity and prenatal care, fertility, menopause, contraception, gynecological surgery, psychology, nutrition, laboratory studies, vaccines and lactation support, delivered across six physical clinics (Tlalpan, Coapa, Del Valle, Polanco, San Angel and Satelite) and through Portal Plenna, a patient portal and iOS/Android mobile app for scheduling appointments, virtual consultations, test results, prescriptions and pregnancy tracking. Plenna is a 500 Global portfolio company. It is surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

name: Plerk
description: Plerk was a Mexican fintech startup offering an employee-benefits and perks platform ("beneficios para colaboradores") for companies in Mexico, backed by 500 Global. During 2023 Plerk merged with minu to consolidate the employee benefits offering in Mexico, and the standalone Plerk product was wound down. Its primary domain plerk.com no longer resolves (DNS fully lapsed; last web archive May 2023) and plerk.io redirects to the now-defunct plerk.com. Support was handled at soporte@plerk.io. This profile is retained as a defunct/acquired lead; the surviving product and any API surface live under minu. No live developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface exists for Plerk.

name: Prescrypto
description: Prescrypto is an electronic-prescription (eRx) platform used across Mexico and LATAM, backed by 500 Global. Its REST Integration API lets EHRs, hospital systems, telemedicine apps and pharmacies manage medics, hospitals, patients and prescriptions; generate legally-valid electronic prescriptions that are verified against Mexico's NOM-151-SCFI-2016 standard via the RexChain blockchain notary; download prescription PDFs; and let pharmacies search and dispense (burn) prescribed medications. The platform also ships a Deeplink auto-login/auto-fill flow, a standard-drug catalog search of ~25,000 records, webhooks for prescription events, and a prescrypto-elements web-component library for embedding Rx functionality in a host site. Authentication is HTTP Token auth (Authorization: Token <key>).

name: Reliv
description: Reliv is a digital medical ecosystem operating in Ecuador and Mexico that aims to simplify healthcare management for clinics, hospitals, doctors, and patients. Its platform combines a Hospital Information System (HIS) for hospital and clinic operations, an Electronic Health Record (EHR) offering digital clinical histories with online scheduling and electronic prescriptions, and a patient-facing Pacientes mobile app for appointments, digital prescriptions, and offers. Reliv positions itself as the first integrated digital medical ecosystem of Ecuador and runs a Reliv Academy training platform. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface was found during enrichment.

name: RUUT
description: RUUT (ruut.mx) is a Mexican fintech and mobile-first investment platform that lets everyday people invest in the US stock markets. Marketed as "la plataforma de inversion para no inversionistas" (the investment platform for non-investors), it gives users access to 8,000+ US stocks and ETFs, personalized risk-based portfolios (safe, moderate, aggressive), goal-based investing, and AI-tailored market news. Accounts are protected up to $500,000 USD via SIPC insurance through its US brokerage partner Alpaca Securities LLC (FINRA/SIPC). RUUT is registered with Mexico's CNBV as an independent investment advisor (Folio #30174) and is a portfolio company of 500 Global. RUUT is a consumer product with no public developer API; this profile was enriched from its public website and live domain probes.

name: Scouter
description: Scouter is a Mexican online marketplace, founded in 2021 in Guadalajara, for discovering and booking unique locations — houses, mansions, studios, terraces, haciendas, rooftops and more — for audiovisual productions, events, photo shoots and workshops across Mexico. It connects brands, agencies and production companies with the owners of over 1,500 spaces, handling quotes and reservations directly via WhatsApp (no public list prices, 8-hour minimum booking). Clients have included Netflix, HBO, Puma, Nike and Grupo Modelo. Backed by 500 Global (500 LatAm "Somos Lucha" Batch 16). The public product is a consumer/host web app at wearescouter.com; it exposes no public developer API. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched.

name: Sofia
description: Sofía is a 100% Mexican digital health insurance company that modernizes traditional medical coverage for enterprises, individuals, and families. Its plans combine zero-deductible major and minor medical care, preventive care with an assigned primary-care physician, and unlimited no-cost video consultations, all managed through a mobile app and an HR administrative portal. Sofía operates its own integrated medical network (SofíaMed) of hospitals and specialists, offers add-ons such as maternity, mental health, dental, and international coverage, and reimburses claims in an average of five business days. Backed by Ribbit Capital, Sofía positions insurance as a digital-first, member-centric health experience rather than a paper policy.

name: Sportwey
description: Sportwey is a Mexican SaaS platform that digitizes and automates the operations of sports organizations across multiple segments — tournaments and leagues, training academies, and sports facilities. It provides team management, scheduling, results and statistics, attendance and membership tracking, payments, class scheduling, court and field reservations, and referee coordination. The company reports more than 10,000 organizers and 2.3 million players using the platform, delivered through dedicated player and referee apps and a manager back office. Sportwey is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, or API documentation.

name: Stori
description: Stori is a Mexico City–headquartered fintech (operating as a regulated Sociedad Financiera Popular under CNBV and CONDUSEF oversight) on a mission to democratize credit access for the roughly 400 million underbanked consumers in Latin America. Founded in 2019, the company achieved unicorn status in 2022 and has raised over $400M from investors including GGV Capital, General Catalyst, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Goodwater Capital, Source Code Capital, Vision Plus Capital, BAI Capital, Tresalia, and GIC. Stori's flagship product is the Stori Card, an inclusive Visa credit card marketed to first-time borrowers with little or no formal credit history, alongside Stori Black (premium tier), co-branded cards (SHEIN, Farmacias Similares, sports teams), Cuenta+ (a commission-free deposit account advertising up to 15% annual returns), personal loans up to roughly $3,000 MXN-equivalent, and payment services covering bill pay, mobile recharges, and phone-based merchant collection. The platform is delivered exclusively through its iOS and Android mobile apps and serves more than five million Mexican users. Stori has no public developer API, SDK, CLI, webhook surface, or open-source release; its revenue model is interest, interchange, and fee income from consumer credit and deposit products, with operations in Mexico, Colombia, and a U.S. corporate presence in Arlington, Virginia.

name: Super Seguros
description: Super Seguros (super.mx) is a Mexican insurtech that lets people quote, buy, and manage insurance entirely online. Its developer product, Super Studio, is a set of REST APIs partners use to generate insurance quotes and sell policies — covering life insurance (12-month term and 5-year plans with savings), home, renters, and landlord products. Quoting endpoints are broadly available and return prefilled purchase links to super.mx; purchase endpoints let approved partners sell insurance directly via API. Authentication is via an X-Api-Key header, with separate sandbox and production hosts. Super Seguros is backed by Anthemis.

name: Syntage
description: Syntage is a Mexican fintech data platform that aggregates business and fiscal data from official Mexican sources (the SAT tax authority, RPC, RUG, credit bureaus / Buro de Credito, and blacklists) into a single API and dashboard. Financial institutions use it to analyze credit risk, verify CFDI invoices for factoring operations, run KYB/KYC/PLD compliance checks, and monitor taxpayer data changes in real time. Data is consumable via a REST API (JSON-LD / Hydra), an app dashboard, PDF reports, and Excel exports. Reported scale includes 300+ financial-institution clients and billions of transactions processed. ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified.

name: TAXO
description: Taxo (Contadores del Futuro) is an AI-powered tax and accounting automation platform for accountants and firms (despachos) in Ecuador and Mexico, used by 2,000+ practices. It automates fiscal work across two regional hubs: Ecuador (integrated with the SRI) and Mexico (integrated with the SAT). Products include bulk invoice/CFDI download bots, AI-assisted tax declarations, electronic invoicing (facturación electrónica / CFDI 4.0 timbrado), invoicing by WhatsApp, batch and mass issuance, and white-label REST APIs (Taxo API, SRI API, SAT API) for embedding electronic invoicing and tax-authority queries into fintechs, e-commerce, ERPs and marketplaces. Backed by 500 Global.

name: Tecnológico de Monterrey
description: Tecnológico de Monterrey (ITESM) is a private Mexican multi-campus university system headquartered in Monterrey, ranked #185 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. It operates a public API developer portal at api.tec.mx that exposes institutional API products (such as student grade/academic-progress, student management, human-capital management, and billing APIs) behind registration and subscription approval, and a public Dataverse-based research open-data repository at datahub.tec.mx run by its Institute for the Future of Education, which serves a public Native REST API and an OAI-PMH metadata endpoint.

name: Ualá
description: Ualá is a Latin American fintech founded in Argentina in 2017 by Pierpaolo Barbieri, offering a neobank super-app (prepaid and credit cards, savings, investments, loans, insurance) in Argentina and Mexico, where it operates as Ualá ABC through the acquired ABC Capital bank. Its merchant arm, Ualá Bis, provides payments acceptance — link de pago, POS, e-commerce plugins, and the API Cobros Online v2, a checkout API with hosted payment links, order retrieval and listing, refunds, and webhook status notifications, documented at developers.ualabis.com.ar with official Node.js and PHP SDKs.

name: Ualá
description: Ualá is an Argentine financial technology company and neobank founded in 2017 by Pierpaolo Barbieri, headquartered in Buenos Aires. The company delivers a mobile-first financial ecosystem anchored by a Mastercard prepaid/debit card linked to an in-app account, with a layered product suite that includes credit cards, personal loans, savings accounts with yield, fixed-term deposits, mutual funds (FCIs), stocks, bonds, CEDEARs, insurance, bill payments, recharges, and international transfers. Its merchant arm, Ualá Bis, provides payment links, online checkout, and POS hardware (POS Mini and POS Pro) for SMBs and online stores, exposing a public Cobros Online v2 API plus SDKs and pre-built integrations for WooCommerce, Tienda Nube, Magento, and Empretienda. Ualá operates as a regulated bank in Argentina (under BCRA oversight), has acquired ABC Capital in Mexico to operate as a chartered Mexican bank, and is the first technology-based company licensed as a financing entity by Colombia's Financial Superintendence. The company reached a $3.2B valuation following $195M in new equity in 2024, and reports more than eight million users across Argentina, Mexico, and Colombia. UaláScore, the company's AI-driven credit evaluation system, powers personalized lending across markets. Public developer surface is limited to the Ualá Bis merchant payments API; the consumer banking, lending, and investing capabilities are not exposed as third-party developer APIs.
